buildUnits.brief:
SCOPE
- `relay(prompt: RelayedPrompt, signal): Promise<boolean>` over an injected `RelayPort`. S5 wires it to the broker's `requestPrompt` in main (work-broker.ts:641-660). It resolves true only on an answer of approved: true.
- It resolves false on any `answered: false` outcome (PROMPT_TIMEOUT, socket dropped or replaced, unit ended, PROMPT_PENDING) and on signal abort. An answer after abort reaches nothing; use the `unlessStopped` pattern (tools.ts:113-130).
- A ToolDestinationPolicy for phone units: isGranted false (per ruling D4); request builds the sheet with mcpSendSheet minus extendedLabel, relays it, and returns 'calls' or 'deny'; onGranted is a no-op.
- A ToolEgressPolicy with no request (local-only target per D2) or relayed (if D2 widens).
- The tool-baked confirms (bash register.ts:23, MCP mcp.ts:178-179) go through `useApp.getState().requestApproval`. In the worker, install `relay` behind an install hook shaped like `installResolver` (app.ts:161-170) rather than rewriting the implementation. Keep the app.ts diff to the hook alone, because sweep-orphans-and-stale-grants also edits app.ts.
- Not-sent records come from the existing dispatcher (#292). Add the `why` reason from the ruling, with exhaustive-switch coverage.

ACCEPTANCE
- An MCP call whose relayed prompt times out never reaches the spy and is recorded not-sent with the ruled why and exact bytes. A later answer is refused and changes nothing.
- The same for a tunnel drop and for cancel.
- Answered yes, the call is sent; the paired control.
- The bash confirm relayed and answered no: nothing runs.
- No 'conversation' grant is ever written (spy on grantMcpEgress).
- No sheet enters `approvals` in the worker.

MUTATIONS
- Resolve true on timeout.
- Keep a late answer.
- Return 'conversation'.
- Skip the not-sent record on expiry.
Each must fail.

MUST STAY TRUE
- A call whose prompt went unanswered never runs later (#170).
- MCP tools stay sensitive.
- No closing keywords in commit text.

buildUnits.name: U4 Worker entry and module-cache isolation audit
dependsOn: U1 Runner core: snapshot in, chunks out, no chat row
U2 Phone policy objects and the relay hook
blockedOnDecisions: Model reach
What the phone-policy tool setting admits
#296 desktop-side fallback

risks: Blocking. Until #296's fallback is ruled and U5 lands, a worker built through today's useApp.initialize diverts a phone's turn to the desktop's cloud provider on a hot desktop, an open breaker or any local failure (app.ts:298-305; engine.ts:735-762, :800-826, :980-1015). The toast goes to a window nobody sees. S4 must not carry a real turn before then.

Any path that hands the decoded request to Bridge or complete() lets the phone steer the desktop. The codec's 'refuse' rejects only JSON-unsafe values (codec/index.ts:210-247), so custom.toolIds enables desktop tools (tools.ts:250-257) and custom.local steers the pressure check (resilience.ts:187-193). The runner must go through engine.stream, which rewrites custom (engine.ts:1356-1367).

Retry runs on the streamed path too: aimatey-middleware 0.2.3 retry.js:78-86 has no streaming guard, and aimatey-core 0.4.0 retries a failure raised before the first chunk (middleware-stack.js:151-155). A desktop-served phone turn's retryable local failure is re-run once (engine.ts:570-577). #152 records 'retry allowed' only as a recommendation, so pin whichever behaviour is chosen.

Cross-owner side channel: the native host reuses the KV prefix on the one shared handle and reports cachedTokens (inference-node llama-cpp.ts:577-596). The number reveals how much of a phone's prompt matched the previous owner's, the desktop user's included, unless it is stripped before crossing.

State carried between units: the bash shell's /workspace (tool.ts:39, :86; index.ts:304), the per-renderer MCP client sessions (client.ts:44-46), and the Router breaker and latency state (engine.ts:510-517). One phone's actions can shape the next phone's turn.

Bash reach: a phone's bash as-is reads every desktop conversation through /chats (stores.ts:47-56) and the desktop person's OS-chooser mounts (tool.ts:92-103). It can also ask to delete a desktop model or open a chat (commands.ts:368-447). Relayed prompts would let the phone approve desktop state changes, which is not covered by '#170 tools the desktop has already enabled' as ruled.

Storage sharing: a worker created with createWindow's webPreferences (main.ts:658-664) shares session.defaultSession IndexedDB with the user's window. Any App-style boot runs load/openChat sweeps against the user's rows. The sweep-orphans-and-stale-grants branch (963cb91) treats another open window as a reason to skip deleting images, and a long-lived worker could defer those sweeps.

The record tension: #170 says 'recorded on the desktop' and #7 ruling 2 says 'nothing stored on the desktop'. An McpCallReceipt holds exact argument bytes (#292), so the wrong reading puts phone conversation bytes into desktop rows.

The broker allows one pending prompt per unit (work-broker.ts:645). This relies on the dispatcher raising sheets one at a time (#292: 'every sheet in a batch is answered before any call runs'). A future parallel dispatch would be refused PROMPT_PENDING and recorded not-sent. Verify with a test, not by reading.

The worker's call path is not built. A runner in src/ cannot construct HostRuntime, and the preload has no MessagePort path (BACKGROUND-WORK-MEASUREMENTS.md:170-207, preload.ts:33-41). Whether a crashed renderer's port emits close is unmeasured. Write S4 against an injected RelayPort and stream sink so S5 can choose the transport.

Merge collisions: stopped-empty-reply (37040cc) edits src/state/chat.ts, domain/chat.ts, MessageView and shell/commands.ts; sweep-orphans-and-stale-grants edits chat.ts (+255), app.ts (+31) and mcp.ts (+7). Keep S4 out of chat.ts and limit app.ts to one install hook. Build the combination before merging more than one.

#293 item 4 is half stale (the provider sheet already takes the signal at chat.ts:1584-1606). Update the issue when U3 lands rather than reporting both halves fixed. #296's body line 'lives outside src/' is superseded by #7 ruling 1 and should be corrected on the issue by the owner.

Provenance: chat.ts:1291 turns reach back into a boolean, and nothing writes 'paired' (domain/chat.ts:103, :156). If the runner spreads the desktop's metadata into the terminal, the phone will print 'On device' for a desktop reply (#213). Use withUpstreamProvenance.
